translation:
For any types X and Y and any N : S1 X Y, call the elements of N.A1 nodes. A directed step from m to n means that there exist two state assignments σ and σ′ and an input x in X such that the assignments agree at every node other than m, but the updates N.a5 n σ x and N.a5 n σ′ x differ. The assignments need not be reachable from the initial state. A path here is a chain of one or more directed steps; a path of length zero does not count.

D11(N) defines the proposition that the node type is nonempty and that, for every node m and every node n, there exists a path from m to n. This includes m = n: every node must have a positive-length path back to itself, though it need not have a direct step to itself.

D12(N) defines the proposition that, for every node m and every node n, if m ≠ n then it is not the case that there is both a path from m to n and a path from n to m. For distinct nodes, one direction or neither may exist. No nonemptiness condition is imposed, and a direct step from a node to itself is not forbidden.

d13(N) defines a natural number: the number of elements of the finite node type N.A1.

divergences.description: D11 requires feedback throughout the whole network: a recurrent core with a one-way output unit would fail its test. P-D52b does not specify all-pairs reachability for the recurrent systems it discusses. This is the author's stated modeling choice, not a characterization of ϕ > 0.

judgement.summary: D11 matches the stated structural proxy, including the requirement of a positive-length return path for each unit. On the finite unit set, D12 is equivalent to the existence of an ordering with no later-to-earlier influence, while allowing self-dependence; d13 counts the units exactly.
